source.heading: The pre-build & the build-on-commit hook
source.text:
## The pre-build & the build-on-commit hook

`dist/web-tools.js` is **the pre-build**: the whole `lib/` frozen into one self-booting offline artifact, so a page adopts the library with one import instead of a `gh.load` chain. `dist/app.js` is the app's own: only what `app/index.html` reaches. Both are tracked. See [`node/README.md`](node/README.md#the-pre-build).

The `gh.load` chain it replaces is the repo's default, not a legacy path. [`docs/loader.md`](docs/loader.md) is the only statement of the contract a file must honor to be loadable that way, plus the timing invariants the boot sequence depends on. Read it before adding a file to `lib/` or changing how a page boots. Which folder the file belongs in is answered in [`docs/code-layers.md`](docs/code-layers.md) and measured by `npm run code-scan`.

Every **deterministic** derived artifact is owned by one commit-time hook, [`.githooks/pre-commit`](.githooks/pre-commit). Before a `git commit` it regenerates and stages, in the same commit, whatever the pending changes touch. [`node/README.md`](node/README.md#the-refresh-model) lists the legs, the order they run in, and why that order matters.

Don't hand-edit a file the hook writes; edit the source and let the hook refresh it. Thumbnails (`pages/thumbs/*.png`) are the exception (see "Per-session refresh" above).

**Git owns the hook, not Claude:** a `PreToolUse` hook disappears when the session root sits above this repo. Run `npm run setup` once per checkout for hooks, the CSV merge driver, and dependencies; `npm run ready` checks without writing. Claude's startup scripts delegate to that shared path. `--no-verify` bypasses it. Details: [extending.md](docs/environment/extending.md).

**Verification stays independent.** Setup never regenerates tracked artifacts, and API, MCP, or server-side writes cannot run local hooks. [`node/test/derived-artifacts.test.mjs`](node/test/derived-artifacts.test.mjs) therefore checks every generator under `npm test`. Repair hook-owned output with `npm run artifacts:refresh`, then run any additional command the test names. A local merge that restamps its combined index pauses for the gated `git -c core.editor=true merge --continue` path.

[`.github/workflows/test.yml`](.github/workflows/test.yml) runs `npm test` on every pull request and reports it as a check on the PR, so the test speaks even when no session runs the suite. `page-measures.yml` also runs on pull requests that touch a page, but only reports: a finding never fails it, so a red run is a fault in the pass, not in a page. The suite is browser-free by construction (`node --test` globs `node/test/**/*.test.mjs`, and every Playwright-driven check is named without `.test.`), so keep it that way or the runner grows a browser install. `package-lock.json` is gitignored, so CI resolves dependency ranges fresh on each run and a green check is not a claim about a pinned tree.

problems.note: The heading calls it the build-on-commit hook, P4 the commit-time hook, P5 and P6 the hook; CLAUDE.md elsewhere says the commit hook. Nothing links the heading's name to P4's.

node/README.md#the-pre-build says third-party libraries (Tailwind, daisyUI, Phosphor, Alpine, CodeMirror) stay on their CDN tags, and its comparison line reads 'whole library, one fetch, no own-code network'. 'Offline' promises more than the file delivers.
The chain is never explained. docs/loader.md: a loader-based page calls gh.load(...) once per component and kit, and each file is fetched and run at runtime.
'Reaches' is node/README.md's term of art and 'what' has no noun: the set is lib files only, found by string-literal paths and x-data component names, transitively.
It says nothing about why the two files are committed or what keeps them current. The hook that does is introduced two paragraphs later, and P4 never says the dist files are among its artifacts.
'it' has no single referent: the previous sentence is a pointer to node/README.md, and the candidates are dist/web-tools.js, dist/app.js and the pre-build.

problems.quote: Which folder the file belongs in
problems.note: 'The file' has no single referent: the previous sentence is about adding a file to lib/, so the folder is already named. docs/code-layers.md decides among lib/, lib/kits/, lib/alpineComponents/, lib/ops/, python/ and node/.

docs/code-layers.md calls code-scan advisory: it counts, per folder, the files any document names and any test exercises (python/unclaimed-code.py). It does not check placement. Placement is checked by python/code-shape.py (npm run code-shape) through node/test/code-layers.test.mjs.

The term is never defined here; the reader has to guess it means P2's dist files. node/README.md#the-refresh-model defines the split: a derived artifact is refreshed one of two ways, by whether its generator is deterministic.
'Legs' is never introduced. They are the hook's separate regeneration steps, headed '# --- leg' in .githooks/pre-commit and tabulated in node/README.md.

problems.quote: Don't hand-edit a file the hook writes
problems.note: Too broad: node/README.md#the-refresh-model says docs/docs.csv, docs/harness.csv, docs/registries.csv and docs/tests-authored.csv are hand-edited except for the fields or rows a generator writes.

The exception is to nothing stated. After 'Don't hand-edit' it reads as leave to hand-edit PNGs; the rule it excepts is P4's claim that the hook owns every deterministic derived artifact. Thumbnails are not deterministic, so the hook only warns (.githooks/pre-commit, leg thumb-nudge).

problems.quote: a `PreToolUse` hook disappears when the session root sits above this repo
problems.note: The reader is not told what a PreToolUse hook is, that this hook was one until 2026-08-06, or what the session root is. As written the clause is a non-sequitur after 'Git owns the hook'. 'Session root' and 'project root' (node/README.md) also name one thing twice.
Which driver is not said. It is derived-csv, registered by npm run setup and named in .gitattributes (node/README.md#the-refresh-model).

'Path' reads as a file path. It means the setup code that npm run setup runs: session-githooks.sh and session-start.sh call node/checkout-setup.mjs (docs/environment/extending.md#sessionstart-checkout-delegates).
'it' could be the shared path of the previous sentence, and the flag is bare. It is `git commit --no-verify` and it bypasses the hook.
Independent of what is never said. The next two sentences show it is independent of the hook and of setup, which may not have run.

One kind of file has four names in this section: 'derived artifact' (P4), 'a file the hook writes' (P5), 'tracked artifacts' and 'hook-owned output' (P7). 'Setup' is also the unglossed npm run setup of P6.

node/test/derived-artifacts.test.mjs holds twelve --check tests. The console build, tests registry, docs registry and CSV census are pinned by node/test/console-suite.test.mjs, tests-registry.test.mjs, docs-registry.test.mjs and csv-census.test.mjs, so the file does not check every generator, though the suite does.

problems.quote: A local merge that restamps its combined index pauses for the gated
problems.note: 'Restamps', 'combined index' and 'gated' are undefined, the agent that restamps (the hook) is left out, and the sentence is about the hook's behavior in a merge, not about verification. node/README.md#the-refresh-model ('Automatic local merge commits use the same order') owns it.

A pull request that cannot merge has no merge ref, so no pull_request run starts (test.yml header, PR #413). The workflow also runs on pushes to main and to session branches (claude/**, codex/**, gemini/**, agent/**), which is the backstop.

problems.quote: so the test speaks even when no session runs the suite
problems.note: 'The test' here is the whole suite (`npm test`), but in P7 'the test' is the one file derived-artifacts.test.mjs; 'speaks' is figurative and 'the suite' follows in the same clause.

problems.quote: a finding never fails it, so a red run is a fault in the pass, not in a page
problems.note: Never says what page-measures does, what a finding is, or what the pass is. .github/workflows/page-measures.yml: it renders touched pages in headless Chromium and reports sideways scroll, blank icons, empty tables and the like; it goes red only when the pass itself is broken.

problems.quote: or the runner grows a browser install
problems.note: 'The runner' could be node's test runner; it means the CI machine, and 'grows' is figurative. The install step would have to download a browser.

problems.quote: a claim about a pinned tree
problems.note: 'Pinned tree' is jargon for a fixed set of dependency versions, which a lockfile would give. .github/workflows/test.yml: no lockfile to npm ci against.

ideas.idea: P4 to P7 read as a description of the hook, so a session has to work out the rules from it. Rewrite them as four actions (commit normally, never hand-edit generated output, run setup once per checkout, repair stale output and check the merge), each opening with its verb, and move the legs, the reasons and the PreToolUse history to the linked documents, which already own them.
ideas.rewrite:
- **Edit the source and commit as usual.** Before each `git commit`, [`.githooks/pre-commit`](.githooks/pre-commit) regenerates and stages, in the same commit, every **deterministic** derived artifact (a committed file generated from other files, such as `dist/web-tools.js`) that the pending changes touch. The steps are listed in [node/README.md](node/README.md#the-refresh-model).

- **Never hand-edit a generated file or field the hook writes.** Thumbnails (`pages/thumbs/*.png`) are derived but not deterministic, so the hook only warns about them. Regenerate them once per session before a merge (see "Per-session refresh" above).

- **Run `npm run setup` once per checkout.** It installs the hooks, the `derived-csv` merge driver and dependencies, and it never regenerates derived artifacts. The commit hook is a git hook, not a Claude Code hook; [extending.md](docs/environment/extending.md) gives the reason. Claude's startup scripts call the same setup script. `npm run ready` checks without writing, and `git commit --no-verify` bypasses the hook.

- **Repair stale output, then check.** `npm test` checks most generators in [`derived-artifacts.test.mjs`](node/test/derived-artifacts.test.mjs), independently of the hook, which `--no-verify` bypasses and API, MCP, or server-side writes cannot run. Repair stale output with `npm run artifacts:refresh`, then run any additional command the test names. When a local merge stops because the hook changed files, finish it with `git -c core.editor=true merge --continue`.
ideas.why: The reader sees a run-book, not a system report: each paragraph now names the action a session takes. node/README.md#the-refresh-model owns the legs and their order, extending.md owns the Claude hook scope, and derived-artifacts.test.mjs owns the check, so CLAUDE.md keeps the rules and links the mechanism. The hook is a git hook and setup never regenerates (checkout-setup.mjs), both as the passage says. Thumbnails stay the one exception, and "only" and "never" survive verbatim.

ideas.idea: P2 gives the reader the adoption step as one import of dist/web-tools.js, with the worked example linked, and says what dist/app.js leaves out: five heavy kits (annotate, pdf, dictate, xlsx, redact) load on first use and are not in the bundle. "Reaches" becomes "uses", and "tracked" becomes "committed".
ideas.rewrite: `dist/web-tools.js` is **the pre-build**: the whole `lib/` frozen into one self-booting artifact that needs no network for the library's own code. A page adopts the library with one `import` of that file, instead of a chain of per-file `gh.load` calls ([`pages/demos/prebuild-demo.html`](pages/demos/prebuild-demo.html) is the worked example). `dist/app.js` is the app's own: the `lib/` files that `app/index.html` uses, directly or through other files, except five heavy kits (`annotate`, `pdf`, `dictate`, `xlsx`, `redact`) that load on first use. Both are committed, and the commit-time hook below rebuilds them. See [`node/README.md`](node/README.md#the-pre-build).
ideas.why: node/README.md#the-apps-pre-build says app/index.html imports dist/app.js and that five kits are left out on purpose; build-app.mjs holds them in LAZY, so a reader adding one of those kits to the app should expect it to load at runtime. The adoption action needs the one import, which node/README.md#the-pre-build gives. Side note outside this lens: the demo's default import, ../dist/web-tools.js, resolves from pages/demos/ to pages/dist/, which does not exist, so the demo's non-?use path looks broken.

ideas.idea: P8 opens with the browser-free naming rule, the one a session breaks by accident, and gives its example file. The page-measures sentence adds the action the report implies: read the job summary, because a green run can still carry findings.
ideas.rewrite: A check that drives a browser through Playwright is named without `.test.` (`node/test/subject-actions.mjs`, not `subject-actions.test.mjs`), because `node --test` globs `node/test/**/*.test.mjs` and the suite has to stay browser-free, or CI has to download a browser. [`.github/workflows/test.yml`](.github/workflows/test.yml) runs `npm test` on every mergeable pull request and reports it as a check on the PR, so the suite reports even when no session runs it. [`page-measures.yml`](.github/workflows/page-measures.yml) also runs on pull requests that touch a page, but only reports: a finding (such as sideways scroll) never fails it. Read the page-measures run's job summary for findings, and treat a red page-measures run as a fault in its measuring pass, not in a page. `package-lock.json` is gitignored, so CI resolves dependency ranges fresh on each run and a green check is not a claim about pinned dependency versions.
ideas.why: The rule that protects the suite (name browser checks without .test.) matters most to a session writing a test, so it leads. test.yml and page-measures.yml confirm the trigger and report-only facts: page-measures publishes the report as the run's job summary, and findings never turn the run red. The lockfile sentence is kept because package-lock.json is gitignored (.gitignore) and test.yml runs npm install.

ideas.idea: Delete P8 entirely. Its CI facts are restated from the headers of .github/workflows/test.yml and .github/workflows/page-measures.yml, and its one failing premise, that the suite runs on every pull request, can be repaired only by deleting the paragraph.
ideas.why: Every fact in P8 has an owner. The header of .github/workflows/test.yml gives the trigger, the reason a pull request that cannot merge gets no run (PR #413), the browser-free rule with its reason (every Playwright check is named without .test. and stays a manual run), and the gitignored package-lock.json. The header of .github/workflows/page-measures.yml says it is report only (Findings never turn this red) and goes red only when the pass itself is broken, which is the one rule a reader acts on: a red run means fix the pass, not the page. The premise fails: test.yml does not run on every pull request, since a pull request that cannot merge has no merge ref and so no pull_request run starts. Repairing that inside 126 words would restate the workflow header, so the repair is the cut. The negations P8 carries (never, only, no) survive verbatim in those headers. The one thing P8 alone says is that CI runs npm test on pull requests; the on: block of test.yml states it, and node/README.md (The refresh model) states it too. That README section is already stale: it lists pushes to main only, while test.yml also runs on pushes to claude/**, codex/**, gemini/**, and agent/** branches.

ideas.idea: Say why the two dist files are tracked: GitHub Pages serves main as-is with no build step, so a page loads the committed copy, and the commit-time hook has to stage the rebuilt file in the same commit as the lib/ change.
ideas.rewrite: Both are tracked because GitHub Pages serves `main` as-is, with no build step, so a page loads the committed copy; the commit-time hook below rebuilds them when `lib/` changes.

## The pre-build & the commit-time hook

`dist/web-tools.js` is **the pre-build**: all of `lib/` in one self-booting file, with no network for the library's own code, replacing a chain of per-file `gh.load(...)` calls. `dist/app.js` holds only the `lib/` files that `app/index.html` uses. Both are tracked and rebuilt by the commit-time hook ([`node/README.md`](node/README.md#the-pre-build)).

The `gh.load` chain is still the repo's default, not a legacy path. [`docs/loader.md`](docs/loader.md) is the only statement of the contract a file must honor to load that way, so read it before adding a file to `lib/` or changing how a page boots. [`docs/code-layers.md`](docs/code-layers.md) says which folder a new file belongs in.

Every **deterministic** derived artifact, a committed file generated from source, is refreshed by one commit-time hook, [`.githooks/pre-commit`](.githooks/pre-commit), which stages it in the same commit. Never hand-edit a generated file: edit its source. Four `docs/` CSVs take hand edits outside their generated fields. Thumbnails (`pages/thumbs/*.png`) are not deterministic, so the hook only warns about them.

Run `npm run setup` once per clone or linked worktree: it installs the hooks, the `derived-csv` merge driver and dependencies. `npm run ready` checks without writing. `git commit --no-verify` bypasses the hook.

`npm test` checks generated output against its source, since `--no-verify` bypasses the hook and server-side writes never run it ([`derived-artifacts.test.mjs`](node/test/derived-artifacts.test.mjs)). Repair with `npm run artifacts:refresh`, then any extra command the test names. If the hook stops a local merge, finish it with `git -c core.editor=true merge --continue`.

CI runs `npm test` on each mergeable pull request and each push to `main` or a session branch ([`test.yml`](.github/workflows/test.yml)). [`page-measures.yml`](.github/workflows/page-measures.yml) only reports: a finding never fails it, so a red run is a fault in its pass, not in a page. ## The pre-build & the commit-time hook

`dist/web-tools.js` is **the pre-build**: all of `lib/` in one self-booting file, so a page loads the whole library with one import instead of a `gh.load` call per file. `dist/app.js` holds only the `lib/` files that `app/index.html` names, directly or transitively. Before adding a file to `lib/`, read [`docs/loader.md`](docs/loader.md) for the contract a file must meet.

[`.githooks/pre-commit`](.githooks/pre-commit) regenerates `dist/web-tools.js` and `dist/app.js`, and any other deterministic derived file whose source changed, into the same commit. Thumbnails (`pages/thumbs/*.png`) are not deterministic, so the hook only warns about them. Don't hand-edit what a generator writes: change the source and let the hook refresh it.

It is a git hook, not a Claude Code hook, so it fires even when a session's project root sits above this repo. Run `npm run setup` once per clone to install the hook; setup never regenerates anything. `git commit --no-verify` bypasses the hook, which is why [`test.yml`](.github/workflows/test.yml) runs `npm test` on every mergeable pull request: stale output fails that check. Repair the output with `npm run artifacts:refresh`.

Both are tracked, and the commit-time hook below rebuilds them. See [`node/README.md`](node/README.md#the-pre-build).

The `gh.load` chain the pre-build replaces is the repo's default, not a legacy path. [`docs/loader.md`](docs/loader.md) is the only statement of the contract a file must honor to be loadable that way, plus the timing invariants the boot sequence depends on. Read it before adding a file to `lib/` or changing how a page boots. Which folder a new code file belongs in is answered in [`docs/code-layers.md`](docs/code-layers.md) and enforced under `lib/` by `npm run code-shape` and `node/test/code-layers.test.mjs`.

Every **deterministic** derived artifact (a committed file generated from other files, such as `dist/web-tools.js`) is owned by one commit-time hook, [`.githooks/pre-commit`](.githooks/pre-commit). Before a `git commit` it regenerates and stages, in the same commit, whatever the pending changes touch. [`node/README.md`](node/README.md#the-refresh-model) lists the hook's legs (its separate regeneration steps), the order they run in, and why that order matters.

Run `npm run setup` once per checkout for hooks, the `derived-csv` merge driver, and dependencies; `npm run ready` checks without writing. Claude's startup scripts delegate to that same setup. `git commit --no-verify` bypasses the hook. Details: [extending.md](docs/environment/extending.md).

**Verification stays independent of the hook.** `npm run setup` never regenerates derived artifacts, and API, MCP, or server-side writes cannot run local hooks. [`node/test/derived-artifacts.test.mjs`](node/test/derived-artifacts.test.mjs) therefore checks most generators under `npm test`. [`.github/workflows/test.yml`](.github/workflows/test.yml) runs `npm test` on every mergeable pull request and reports it as a check on the PR, so the suite reports even when no session runs it. `page-measures.yml` also runs on pull requests that touch a page, but only reports: a finding (a defect it measures in a browser, such as sideways scroll) never fails it, so a red run is a fault in its measuring pass, not in a page.
